subject: Acme Health — request for contract exit compensation and termination rights
messages:
From: Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Contract exit compensation / SLA exceptions — Acme Health position

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward finalizing the Dedicated commitment, our procurement and legal teams have flagged a hard requirement we need included in the contract: remedies that go beyond service credits.

High level ask from Acme: if Redwood misses the committed availability/latency SLOs in a material way (multiple high-severity incidents impacting production), Acme must have an express right to terminate for convenience and recover an exit compensation payment — either a fixed buyout (several months of committed fees) or pre-agreed liquidated damages tied to lost operational costs. Credits alone do not address our regulatory and continuity obligations for patient-facing services.

What we attached: Acme_SLA_Exceptions_v3.docx – a short list of exception language and the types of triggers we consider material. Key items: 1) escrow/holdback equal to a portion of committed fees, 2) unilateral termination right after a defined remediation cadence is exhausted, and 3) a capped exit payment as an alternative to extended litigation.

We realize this is atypical for many vendors, so we’re open to structured compromises (e.g., defined cure windows, capped exposure, or a staged exit ladder). We need confirmation on Redwood’s willingness to entertain anything other than credits by end of next week (Nov 9) so procurement can close. Can we schedule a short call with legal to run through the wording?

Thanks,
Taylor Brooks
Sr. Director, Infrastructure & Ops
Acme Health

Attachment: Acme_SLA_Exceptions_v3.docx (docx, 28 KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract exit compensation / SLA exceptions — Acme Health position

Taylor — thanks for the clear note and for sharing Acme_SLA_Exceptions_v3. I’ve looped in Grace (Sales lead) and Aditya (Commercial legal) so we can align quickly.

Short answers up front: we understand the concern and the regulatory constraints you're operating under. Redwood’s default position is to provide service credits for SLA shortfalls, plus robust operational guarantees and fallback policies. That said, we can consider limited, structured exit remedies in certain enterprise commitments where there is high sensitivity.

Potential compromise options we’re prepared to discuss next week (high level):
- Stepwise remediation ladder: credits + mandatory remediation actions + independent verification.
- Termination for convenience only after repeated, unremediated severity-1 incidents within a defined window (e.g., 3 incidents in 90 days) and after a predefined cure period.
- Escrow/holdback: holdback equal to up to 3 months of committed fees payable on termination for the defined triggers.
- Cap on exit compensation: capped to a multiple of monthly committed fees (we can discuss cap sizing — up to 6 months in extreme cases).

We prefer to avoid open-ended liquidated damages, but are willing to negotiate a narrow, contractually capped exit payment tied to objective triggers. If that sounds like a reasonable starting point, let’s set a 30-minute call with your legal/procurement and Aditya to iterate language. I’ll prepare a short addendum draft that maps to the bullets above (and will include audit rights and additional evidence requirements to ensure consistency).

Availability: Tue/Wed next week 9–11am PT or Thu 3–5pm PT.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Acme Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract exit compensation / SLA exceptions — Acme Health position

Jonas / Redwood team,

Following up from Taylor. From Acme Legal's perspective, credits are an operational band‑aid and do not mitigate our compliance and patient safety obligations. If a vendor’s service fails to meet SLOs in a way that meaningfully impairs production, Acme needs:

1) A contractual right to terminate without penalty;
2) A defined exit payment equal to no less than six months of historical average monthly spend (to cover transition and remediation costs); or
3) A pre-agreed liquidated damages formula tied to measurable business impact (we proposed a simple multiplier in the attached doc).

We are open to a capped structure, but not to a regime that leaves Acme exposed to protracted cure cycles while we handle patient impact. We would agree to a short cure window (eg, 7–14 days for certain incidents) but need the termination option preserved if remediation fails.

Quoted below is an excerpt from Taylor’s note for context: 

> "Credits alone do not address our regulatory and continuity obligations for patient-facing services."

Please confirm whether Redwood will accept a holdback/escrow and fixed exit payment as listed above, or whether you will only offer credits and operational remedies. We realize this requires executive sign-off; please advise next steps and timing.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Counsel, Acme Health
legal@acmehealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acmehealth.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract exit compensation / SLA exceptions — Acme Health position

Maya / Taylor — thanks for the direct note and for surfacing the legal viewpoint. We’ve discussed internally (cc: Grace, Aditya) and here’s a concrete compromise we can put into an addendum for signature. This is intended to balance Acme’s need for fast, reliable remediation/transition with Redwood’s risk controls for enterprise commitments.

Proposal (to be captured in Draft_Addendum_Acme_Redwood.pdf):
- Triggers: material remediation trigger = 3 severity-1 or severity-2 production-impact incidents within any 90-day rolling window, where each incident is confirmed by our joint post-incident review.
- Cure: Redwood is granted a defined cure period per incident (standard: 14 days; for certain infra issues we can agree 7 days for immediate hotfix).
- Holdback: Redwood will accept an escrow/holdback equal to three (3) months of committed fees (funded at contract effective date) to be released on contract expiry or paid to Acme on a qualifying termination.
- Exit payment cap: if Acme exercises termination under the defined triggers, the exit compensation will be the greater of (a) the escrowed amount or (b) remaining committed fees prorated up to a maximum of six (6) months of committed MRR. This replaces open-ended liquidated damages.
- Audit & evidence: Acme will have rights to request logs/traces for incidents (subject to agreed access controls and NDAs) and Redwood will provide a post-incident RCA within 3 business days of resolution.
- Transition support: Redwood will provide 30 days of transition assistance (knowledge transfer + best-effort cutover assistance).

Rationale: This avoids open-ended exposure for Redwood, gives Acme immediate financial recourse (holdback) and a capped exit remedy, and preserves our ability to cure issues without immediate contract termination. The escrow is a practical mechanism to ensure funds are available without running to litigation.

Next steps: Aditya will draft the addendum mapping these bullets to contract language and attach Draft_Addendum_Acme_Redwood.pdf for redlines. If Acme confirms this framework is acceptable, we can lock the economic terms and proceed to signatures. If you prefer a different cap sizing or cure cadence, call it out in your redlines and we’ll iterate.

Would you like to meet Wed 11/11 9am PT to review the draft?

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: Draft_Addendum_Acme_Redwood.pdf (pdf, 46 KB)
